display.title: The Mysterious Broom Maker, Part 1
display.summary_short: A Parshas Toldos lesson: a Jew is always a precious diamond. Then Reb Leib Sarah's tries to save the Jews of Kobrin from a poritz who demands years of rent.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens with Parshas Toldos. Why was Rivkah calmed when told she was carrying twins? As Rashi explains, she had felt the child pulled both toward the beis midrash and toward idol worship, and was relieved to learn these were two separate children, Yaakov and Esav. So too, when the yetzer hara tells us we are bad, we must remember that a Jew is always good, like a diamond that only got muddy. Even Esav had great potential, and the Sages tell that his head was buried in the Cave of Machpelah. Like a baby learning to walk, we get up and keep going. The story then begins: Reb Leib Sarah's, born through the Baal Shem Tov's blessing, meets Reb Binyomin of Kobrin in the Berditchev marketplace. The new poritz demands years of back rent his father never asked for and threatens to expel the Jews. Reb Leib urges trust in Hashem and visits the poritz, who offers to cancel the debt if the Jews secretly join a Polish uprising against the Czar. Reb Leib refuses, since the Torah teaches loyalty to the government, and is thrown out. He tells Reb Binyomin they must turn to "plan B". To be continued.
display.lesson: A Jew is always good and precious to Hashem, even after a mistake; get up and keep going. Hashem alone is in charge, so strengthen your bitachon.
